summary: Legion is a programming model and runtime in which logical regions describe data locality and independence, and tasks declare the privileges and coherence with which they access regions. A distributed scheduler extracts parallelism from these declarations, and a mapping interface lets applications control task and memory placement without changing correctness.
why_read: It is the foundational region-based task runtime that later region-based and task-based compilers build on.
main_contribution: A region-based programming model with a distributed software out-of-order scheduler and a mapping interface that separates performance decisions from correctness.
main_limitation: Communication overhead grows with node count in two of the three applications, and the strongest results depend on application-specific mappers.
evaluation_method: Strong and weak scaling on three GPU clusters against hand-coded CUDA, PARSEC and BoxLib references
benchmarks: three-level adaptive mesh refinement heat equation (BoxLib)
states_relationship_to: Bauer et al. 2011, Sequoia for irregular parallelism [10]
